core_requests: P343 FC3: core whois43 helper for PASSIVE third_party modules - ctx.net.whois43(server, query, *, timeout=10.0, max_bytes=65536) -> bytes: TCP 43 only to the IANA root-zone WHOIS server of the queried TLD or one validated referral host (public DNS name, never an IP/internal name), resolved through the DoH/egress profile (no local getaddrinfo), one query line + CRLF, read to EOF or the 64 KB cap (truncation flagged), timeout capped by the run deadline, OfflineError when a proxy is configured or 43/tcp is blocked, 3 s between queries to one server and <= 200 queries per server and day, a request-ledger record per query (method WHOIS). whois_fallback already calls it (getattr) and reports UNAVAILABLE 'offline' until it exists.

P343 FC2: per-source cache TTL in provider extension fragments (or a 7-day ttl for source iana.whois_fallback_root_db): the core-owned iana http_profile caps the HTTP cache at 24 h, so the IANA root-zone answer is kept 7 days in ctx.state instead.

P342 FC3: fold saas_vendors (and saas_unknown_prefixes, the WHOIS attributes registration_* / registrar_whois_server / registry_whois_server, tag saas_footprint) from v3lum/data/vocab/p2-G01-4.json into core/vocab.py if the core list must hold them.
P342 FC1: expose DnsAnswer.truncated (DoH TC=1) or answer TC=1 as could-not-verify in core/dns.py; a module cannot tell a truncated TXT RRset from a complete one.

P342 FC1: single-flight (in-flight de-duplication) of identical DoH queries in the resolver, so dns_records, email_security_posture and saas_verification_tokens never send the same TXT query twice when they miss the cache at the same moment.
P343 FC1 (optional): move the P003 bootstrap helper (bootstrap_lookup, BootstrapMatch, BootstrapUnavailable) from v3lum/modules/domain_dns/rdap.py to v3lum/core and re-export it.
notes: P342 saas_verification_tokens (default on, DoH-only provider core_doh; hosts=() because the council hosts cloudflare-dns.com and dns.google are the core DoH resolvers, implicit per guide s.8): one ctx.dns TXT query (a DoH cache hit after dns_records/email_security_posture, tested), bundled own-work prefix table at v3lum/data/saas_verification_tokens/txt_verification_prefixes.json (module-owned path instead of data/txt_verification_prefixes.json), attribute saas_vendors + saas_unknown_prefixes (prefixes listed raw without values or ids) and ONE info finding with phishing-simulation/ASM hints (IdP, helpdesk, e-signature, security-awareness, other lures); wording 'verification record present'; max_pivots=0; raw TXT strings only in res.raw (evidence). DoH SERVFAIL/timeout/429/challenge -> ERROR/RATE_LIMITED/BLOCKED, never EMPTY. FC5: the recorded gaps__saas_tenants sample held only a json_extract summary (Status 0, Answer.len 98); it is kept and tested as could-not-verify, and the identical request was re-recorded (98 records) with every token value scrubbed. P343 whois_fallback (default on, providers registry_whois [virtual, port 43], iana [+extension source whois_fallback_root_db], whodat_selfhosted [hosts_from_settings whodat_url]): applies() only from the P003 bootstrap helper (no_rdap, rdap_http_only, .br second path only on explicit -M/run of a typed seed); unreadable bootstrap -> UNAVAILABLE dataset. Order: self-hosted who-dat (whodat_url, https only) -> IANA root-zone page (7 days in module state) -> port 43 via the requested core helper (UNAVAILABLE offline in this build; proxy configured -> UNAVAILABLE). One referral hop only for thin registry records at TLP:CLEAR/GREEN with --allow-unknown (registrar WHOIS servers are unknown-tier parties, A8); otherwise recorded in registration_referral. Allow-list parsers drop every contact value at ingestion (tests with the .br who-dat and port-43 samples: no names, e-mails, CNPJ 05.506.560/0001-36 or client IP anywhere in the result or evidence); nameserver pivots only (expand=False), never CNPJ. whois_fallback_public: separate opt-in module for who-dat.as93.net (provider as93, tier unknown, max_tlp green, default off, daily_quota 100, 2 s interval). Terms 'open' for the public instance follow the council's P343 class (MIT code); the hosted service publishes no ToS (backlog row for legal). Hosts: data.iana.org is declared by both P343 modules because the bootstrap dataset download is triggered by them. Port-43 fixtures are synthetic documented layouts (port 43 unreachable here); the who-dat error shapes are synthetic too. No LIGHT/ACTIVE variant was required. Acceptance routes added for domain example.com (saas_verification_tokens EMPTY, whois_fallback not applicable).
